payload.title: Re: [Javamail-crypto-devel] TR: Problem signing emails
payload.author: allen p.
payload.body:
Hi again.

I just posted a new version on SourceForge that cleans up the S/MIME
signing code a little bit.  But it occurred to me after I did that that
there might be another problem going on here.  The BouncyCastle S/MIME
library uses the (relatively) new application/pkcs7-signature MIME type to
identify its signature part.  Apparently some older systems still only
recognize application/x-pkcs7-signature.

So try out the new release and see if it works.  If not, try this new
provider file.  If that works, then I'll clean it up (I'll need to change
the encryption headers, too) and put out yet another release.  :)

-allen


On Mon, Jun 19, 2006, 09:10, Nicolas Zielinski
<nic...@tr...> wrote
>Hi,
>
>> Just to check, is webMethods the only system that's having problems?
>
>Yes, but it's the only that I tested too...
>
>In fact I just send mails to another company that uses webMethods, so I
cannot test it directly either  :/
>
>> Also, are you also using a Thawte free certificate?  And getting
something
>> like a 'issuer's certificate is either unavailable or invalid' message?
>
>Yes but I'm also using a GlobalSign free certificate and the problem is
the same.
>
>I don't have much details about the error, I just have a few precisions
about how webMethods work :
>
>---
>
>webMethods does 2 steps:
>1) verification of the signature
>2) check is the digital certificate chain is trusted
>
>At this moment, we don't pass step 1 when working with your application.
>
>In step 2, to check if the digital certificate chain is trusted, the
system can work in 2 ways:
>
>a) the digital certificate chain is included in the email
>
>b) digital certificate chain isn't included in the email -> in this case,
webMethods will check on the file system for the certificate belonging to
the incoming mail (search for client, intermediate and root certificate) in
a pre-configurated directory.
>
>--
>
>Regards,
>Nicolas.
>
>
